values.Plan and process: AggieTrack, the academic planning and advising platform.
Version 1.0, 12 Oct 2026.
James Allred, developer and technical lead. LaDarius Taylor, testing lead. Mellonie Evans, operations. Ivy Mitchell, user experience.
Check sign-in, the curriculum, course planning, prerequisites and paired courses, advisor work, progress, and search. Keep evidence that can be repeated. Mark each result Pass, Fail, or Blocked.

The team is testing the main student and advisor paths: sign-in, academic requirements, course planning, prerequisite checks, degree progress, and advisor work. The plan covers all 10 functional requirements and all 11 non-functional requirements. A feature that is not built yet stays in the plan and is tested when it exists.

This plan does not cover the student information system, financial aid, tuition, or official transcripts. Approving a plan with a PIN, or a student confirming that they registered, is not official enrollment. Production support is out of scope. Draft file uploads, SAR, and WebSocket targets are not acceptance promises.

The Final Requirement Specs are what we accept against. The seed and the code describe how to set the test up, and what the app does today. A gap in the code does not weaken the requirement. The snapshot is commit e96d249, plus local edits in planner/PlanEditor.tsx, planner/page.tsx, and lib/catalog.ts. See source note R-10.

Use an isolated copy of the real stack: Next.js 16.3.4, React 19.2.8, Prisma 7.10.0, and PostgreSQL through the Neon adapter. Better Auth is the version pinned in the lockfile, from the ^1.7.3 range. Resend mail is caught by the test inbox. Redis was not in the runtime that was reviewed. Write down the exact build, schema, and environment. Do not use real student data, and do not run the seed against production.
LaDarius leads testing. James leads the technical work. The tools are a browser, an API client, a read-only database check, a test inbox, a load generator, a way to cause failures, and monitoring.

Safari, Edge, Firefox, and Chrome. Performance runs at 100 Mbps and at 200 Mbps, with the latency written down. The size of the data set has to be approved, and the machine running the load has to be measured. Screen readers, if Q-16 agrees: VoiceOver with Safari, and NVDA with Firefox.

Use the real merged catalog and curriculum from source notes R-02 and R-05. Do not invent courses. Test people use synthetic names and stay private. Fixture D-04 fixes the clock at 2026-10-11 for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 tests. Use 2026-02-15 when the test needs Spring, Summer, and Fall 2026. Look up course and term ids by code, season, and year. Do not guess an id. Reset only the test student's data, and only in the isolated database.

You need the isolated build, schema, and seed snapshot, verified test accounts, Information Technology and Electronics Technology 2025 profiles, confirmed prior coursework, an advisor assigned in the fixture, the real term rows, and the fixed clock. Review the open decisions on sources, rules, and permissions first. A case may still be run to show a known gap. Mark it Blocked only when the environment or the agreed expected result is missing.

Start with T-01 and T-42 for verification and onboarding. Then T-06, T-07, and T-62 for the catalog. Then T-08 through T-15, plus T-43 through T-49, T-56, T-57, T-58, T-61, and T-72, for validation. Then T-19, T-20, T-21, T-51, T-52, T-59, T-63, T-64, T-65, T-66, T-67, T-69, T-70, and T-71 for progress. Then T-53, T-54, T-55, and T-41 for approval and plan state. Then T-22 through T-29 for access and search, with T-50 and T-60. Then T-16, T-17, and T-18 for the missing advisor workflows. Then T-30 and T-40 for browsers and accessibility. The remaining cases are timing, load, recovery, and encryption.

Every case is Not run after this review of the sources. Pass needs a measured result from the running app or the database, and every agreed check has to hold. Fail means you saw the app break a rule. Blocked means a missing environment, a missing agreed result, or a missing workflow stopped the run. A finding from reading the code is a G item. Do not paste it into Actual result, and do not mark the test Pass or Fail from the code alone. Missing behavior that the requirement asks for does not get acceptance credit.

Every case in scope has been run and passed, with its evidence. There are no open critical or high defects. Any lower defect that remains is accepted in writing by the sponsor. The baseline decisions are resolved, and requirement coverage has been reviewed. A waiver names the scope, the risk, and who approved it. A waiver is not the same as saying the product passed.

When you log a defect, include its id, the build and environment, the test and requirement, the steps, the inputs, what you expected, what happened, the evidence, how severe it is, and who owns the fix. Critical means someone saw data they should not, data was lost, or the app was down. High means a core path is blocked, or degree rules are wrong. Medium means there is a workaround. Low means it is cosmetic. Triage with the test lead and the product owner.

When a fix is ready, write down the new build and link the defect. Reset the same fixture. Repeat the failed case and the nearby boundary tries. Also rerun tests that share the same rule or the same data, plus the smoke set T-01, T-08, T-10, and T-22. Keep the original evidence. Close the defect only after the retest passes and the related checks pass.

Use synthetic data only. Test accounts get the least access they need. Mail stays in the local test inbox. Keep secrets out of this workbook. Remove passwords, tokens, emails, and ids from screenshots and logs. Keep evidence in a restricted store. The proposal is to keep it for 90 days after acceptance, pending Q-15, then delete the fixtures and the evidence under the approved policy.

The source review was read-only. No app tests, database tests, seeds, migrations, or repository edits were run for that review. seed.ts deletes and replaces prerequisite groups and curricula, and it can reassign students. Run it only in a disposable database, after a snapshot. Load and failure tests still need permission, and the stop thresholds from version 1.0 still apply.

Name the evidence with the run id, the test id, and the variant. Include the time in UTC, the tester, the build, the browser and operating system, the seed version, the inputs, screenshots with secrets removed, the API responses, and the relevant database differences and timings. Actual result is what you saw. The evidence reference points at the stored file. Do not invent an outcome.

71 cases cover all 10 functional requirements and all 11 non-functional requirements. The course catalog documents 199 courses the seed can load, plus 3 source rows that are skipped. G-01 through G-14 are findings from reading the code. They are not executed defects. The 500-person test, the daily backup, the encryption evidence, and accessibility on more than one platform still need a staging environment. Fall 2027 is not seeded. Coverage counts come from test status. When a case is added, extend the mapping.

Before this is submitted, the test lead and the academic advisor check every mapping, every expected result, and every fixture. The technical lead checks that the setup can be repeated. The privacy and accessibility owners review the criteria that belong to them. Decisions and owners are recorded under Risks and decisions. At this point every planned test is Not run.

The highlighted cells are filled in while a test is run. On a test, enter the actual result, the status, the defect id, the evidence reference, who ran it, and the date. Write the exact build and environment in the evidence. On a defect, keep the finding and what the retest showed.

values.Test / scenario: Sign up, choose Information Technology 2025, and keep CST 130 on the plan
values.Preconditions: A new email for student A; A test inbox that only this run can see; Fixtures D-01, D-02, and D-04
values.Inputs / data: A test first and last name; student.a@example.test; A password of at least 8 characters; Information Technology, catalog 2025; CST 130, 3 credits
values.Procedure:
1. Choose **Get started**.
2. Enter the **First Name**, **Last Name**, **Email**, and **Password**.
3. Enter the same password in **Verify Password**.
4. Choose **Create Account**.
5. Open the email titled **You're in. Confirm it.**
6. Choose **Confirm your email**.
7. Open **Sign in**.
8. Enter the email and password.
9. Choose **Sign in**.
10. Enter Information Technology in **Search available programs...**.
11. Choose Information Technology.
12. Choose **2025** under **Catalog Year**.
13. Choose **Create Student Profile**.
14. Open **Progress**.
15. Choose **I have no prior coursework**.
16. Open **Planner**.
17. Choose **No, plan Spring 2027**.
18. Choose **Spring 2027**.
19. Enter CST 130 in **Search for a course**.
20. Choose CST 130.
21. Choose **Log Out**.
22. Sign in again.
23. Open **Planner**.
24. Check the result. You should see one CST 130 row on Spring 2027, for 3 credits. The other student's courses are not on this account.
values.Expected result: The account is verified and has the student role; There is one Information Technology 2025 profile; The selected plan has one CST 130 row
values.Pass criterion: Verification and onboarding both finish; After signing in again, CST 130 is still there once, at 3 credits; The other student's data is not on this account
values.Evidence to retain: Screenshots with personal details removed; The account reference; The plan before and after

values.Test / scenario: Turn away a bad login
values.Preconditions: Student A is already verified; The **Sign in** page is available; Each try starts signed out
values.Inputs / data: The right email with the wrong password, at least 8 characters; An email that has no account; A blank email; A blank password; An email that is not a valid address; A password of 7 characters
values.Procedure:
1. Open **Sign in**.
2. Choose **Sign in** with the right email and the wrong password.
3. Choose **Sign in** with an email that has no account.
4. Choose **Sign in** with a blank **Email**.
5. Choose **Sign in** with a blank **Password**.
6. Choose **Sign in** with an email that is not a valid address.
7. Choose **Sign in** with a password of 7 characters.
8. Open **Dashboard** after each rejection.
9. Check the result. You should see each try stays on **Sign in**. No courses or degree progress are shown.
10. Note: A request sent with no session must also be refused, and no course is saved. Keep that response with the secrets removed. No automated test covers the unsigned request list.
values.Expected result: Each bad try is rejected; No session is created; Academic data stays hidden
values.Pass criterion: All six tries are rejected by the form or the server; The protected student page shows no academic data; The protected action returns no academic data
values.Evidence to retain: The responses, with secrets removed; The session state after each try

values.Test / scenario: Reset a password and keep the plan
values.Preconditions: Student A is verified and already has CST 130 saved; The test inbox catches the reset email
values.Inputs / data: Student A's email; The link from that email; A new matching password of at least 8 characters
values.Procedure:
1. Open **Login**.
2. Choose **Forgot password?**.
3. Enter the email.
4. Choose **Send the link**.
5. Open the email titled **Forgot it. Fine.**
6. Choose **Set a new password**.
7. Enter the new password in **New password**.
8. Enter it again in **Verify password**.
9. Choose **Update password**.
10. Choose **Log Out**.
11. Choose **Sign in** with the old password.
12. Choose **Sign in** with the new password.
13. Open **Planner**.
14. Choose **Spring 2027**.
15. Check the result. You should see **You're set.** after the update. The old password is rejected and the new one works. CST 130 is still on the plan.
values.Expected result: The reset finishes; The old password is rejected and the new one works; The saved plan is unchanged
values.Pass criterion: Exactly one reset email arrives; The old password is rejected; The new password is accepted; The saved plan is the same
values.Evidence to retain: The email details, with the token removed; The sign-in results, with secrets removed

values.Test / scenario: Reject a reset link that is expired, reused, or invalid
values.Preconditions: Confirm how long the reset link actually lasts; The email says the link lasts one hour; Use a separate link for each try, and control the clock
values.Inputs / data: A reset link checked at 59 minutes 59 seconds; A reset link checked at 60 minutes 1 second; A link that was already used; A link that was never issued; A password of 7 characters; A confirmation that does not match
values.Procedure:
1. Open one reset link at 59 minutes 59 seconds.
2. Choose **Update password** with a valid new password.
3. Open a different link at 60 minutes 1 second.
4. Use a valid link once.
5. Open that same link again.
6. Open a link that was never issued.
7. Enter a password of 7 characters on **Set a new password**.
8. Enter a confirmation that does not match.
9. Choose **Sign in** with the old password.
10. Choose **Sign in** with the new password.
11. Check the result. You should see a link still inside the hour opens **Set a new password** and finishes. An expired, reused, or invalid link shows **That link is dead.** A short or mismatched password is rejected, and the password does not change.
values.Expected result: A link still inside the hour works; An expired, reused, or invalid link is rejected; A short or mismatched password is rejected
values.Pass criterion: The one-hour promise on the screen matches the real expiry; None of the bad tries change the password; After a successful reset, the old password no longer works
values.Evidence to retain: The error responses, with tokens removed; The time and the expiry that was configured; The sign-in checks

values.Test / scenario: Stop a second account from colliding with the first
values.Preconditions: Student A already has an account and a saved plan
values.Inputs / data: Student A's existing email; The same email with different letter case, if the team has agreed that case should not matter
values.Procedure:
1. Choose **Get started**.
2. Enter the existing email.
3. Choose **Create Account**.
4. Repeat with the same email in different letter case, when that rule is in force.
5. Open **Sign in** on the original account.
6. Open **Planner**.
7. Check the result. You should see a second verified account is not created. The original plan is unchanged. If the first account was not verified yet, another verification email arrives.

values.Pass criterion: There is still one account, and the plan is not merged with another; The original data is unchanged; Write down the verified try and the unverified try separately
values.Evidence to retain: The account count; The plan comparison

values.Test / scenario: Show the Information Technology 2025 handbook and course groups
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-02 is loaded in its own database; The profile is Information Technology and the catalog year is confirmed
values.Inputs / data: Information Technology 2025; The handbook on **Program Outline**; The course list on **Courses**
values.Procedure:
1. Open **Planner**.
2. Open **Program Outline**.
3. Check the 13 requirement groups.
4. Check the 22 named core courses, their credits, and the 8 semesters.

values.Test / scenario: Add a valid course and find it still there after a reload

2. Choose **Spring 2027**.
3. Enter CST 130 in **Search for a course**.
4. Choose CST 130 again.
5. Choose **Reset** for this student on **Test Accounts**.

values.Inputs / data: The CST 130 row on the Spring 2027 plan
values.Procedure:
1. Open **Planner**.
2. Choose **Spring 2027**.
3. Write down the draft and the courses on **Progress**.
4. Choose **Remove CST 130**.
5. Reload **Planner**.
6. Choose **Log Out**.
7. Sign in again.
8. Open **Planner**.
9. Open **Progress**.

values.Test / scenario: Remove a prerequisite that a later course still needs
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-04 sets the clock; Student A has CST 120 on the Fall 2026 draft; CST 112 and CST 122 are on the Spring 2027 draft; MATH 110 is not on the transcript or the plan
values.Inputs / data: Remove CST 120 from Fall 2026, then try to submit and approve Spring 2027
values.Procedure:
1. Open **Planner**.
2. Confirm CST 112 was allowed because CST 120 was planned earlier.
3. Remove CST 120 from Fall.
4. Read the message.
5. Reload Spring 2027.
6. Choose **Submit for review**.
7. Sign in as the assigned advisor.
8. Open **Plans**.
9. Try to approve that plan.
10. Check the result. You should see the removal saved, and a sentence that CST 112 still needs CST 120 or MATH 110 before Spring 2027. Submit and approval of that Spring plan are refused with the same kind of sentence. The message does not show a raw term code.
values.Expected result: Removing CST 120 is saved, and the screen shows a sentence that CST 112 still needs CST 120 or MATH 110 before Spring 2027; Submit and approval of that Spring plan are refused with the same kind of sentence; The message does not show a raw status such as SPRING
values.Pass criterion: CST 112 is never approved when neither CST 120 nor MATH 110 is satisfied; The removal message names the later course; A refused submit or approval does not change the plan status
values.Evidence to retain: The validation message; The plan before and after

values.Test / scenario: Check when a prerequisite counts, including the transcript

3. Add CST 112 with CST 122 to Spring 2027.

values.Test / scenario: An advisor changes an assigned student's plan by hand
values.Preconditions: Advisor Sarah Martinez is assigned to the student; The student is in Information Technology and has a Spring 2027 plan; CST 130 is not on that plan; Gap G-05 is the known missing workflow
values.Inputs / data: The advisor adds CST 130 for the student, then removes it
values.Procedure:
1. Sign in as Sarah Martinez.
2. Open **Plans**.
3. Look for the student's plan.
4. Look for a control that edits the courses by hand.
5. Add CST 130 when that control is there.

values.Baseline requirement (faithful summary): A student signs in with an email and password, and can reset a forgotten password.
A student can see the requirements for their own program.
A student can add a course when it follows the rules.
A student can remove a course from the degree plan.
Each term checks prerequisites and courses that must be taken together before the plan is accepted.
An advisor can change a plan by hand and leave comments.
The app shows how much of the degree is finished, as a percentage. The source document calls this “grade degree.”
A person has to sign in before they can see a plan. The source still says username and password.
When something goes wrong, the person sees an error.
Students and advisors can search for courses that fit that student's situation. The source says the list should include only eligible courses.
The app works in current web browsers.
A page loads within 5 seconds on a 100 to 200 Mbps connection, with up to 500 people using the app at once.
The app signs a person out after 30 minutes with nothing happening.
A person can finish a common task in fewer than 5 clicks.
Data is backed up every day, and a backup can be restored.
Adding or removing a course is saved within 15 seconds, or the person sees an error.
People only see and change what their role allows.
After a failure, the app is usable again within 3 minutes, and academic data that was already saved is still there.
At least 500 people can use the app at once without it slowing down.
Plans and schedules are encrypted, and student data is protected in the way the FERPA note describes.
A person using a keyboard or a screen reader can complete the same tasks. The source points to WCAG.

The acceptance baseline is Functional Requirements.pdf and the Final Requirement Specs, pages 7 to 15. Source notes R-01 through R-10 and the course catalog record the project snapshot. Notes from reading the code are not test results.

values.Issue / risk: Who can edit a plan, and what happens if two people save
values.Source gap or constraint: An assigned advisor can approve a plan; Manual course changes and comments are not built; There is no written rule for student consent or for changing the assigned advisor

values.Issue / risk: What “updates right away” means
values.Source gap or constraint: Some screens refresh after a save; Degree completion is not recalculated live; There is no approved time limit for a live update

values.Issue / risk: When a session ends

values.Issue / risk: What happens when a save is slow or finishes late
values.Source gap or constraint: The planner shows errors and toasts; There is no explicit 15-second deadline; There is no written way to catch a database failure and put the screen back in line with what was saved
values.Proposed control / decision: Measure real save times, timeouts, and a commit that arrives late. Test that a lecture and lab roll back together. Leave the exact error deadline open until it is decided.

values.Issue / risk: What course search is supposed to return
values.Source gap or constraint: The course browser searches the whole curriculum for a matching word; The planner shows eligible courses for the term, needs at least 2 characters, and shows at most 8; An advisor search in the student's context is missing
values.Proposed control / decision: Decide which search has to pass acceptance. Keep the FR-10 expectation of eligible courses, for both roles, as gap G-06. Compare the two searches in T-60.

values.Issue / risk: Which browsers are supported
values.Source gap or constraint: “Modern browsers” is not a list
values.Proposed control / decision: Use the latest stable Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari when the test is run. Write down the version and the operating system, and approve that list.

values.Issue / risk: Whether 500 people at once is realistic
values.Source gap or constraint: The final spec, page 11, limits prototype testing to small groups; There is no agreed limit for how much slower is too slow; The workload and the size of the data are not set
values.Proposed control / decision: Keep the 500-person target. Approve the D-07 workload, the amount of data, how to measure, the tolerance, and whether staging can hold it. If that environment is not available, mark the test Blocked. Do not mark it Pass.

values.Issue / risk: How clicks are counted
values.Source gap or constraint: The tasks and their starting screens are not specified; Keyboard use is not called equivalent; The final spec has no satisfaction target
values.Proposed control / decision: Approve the tasks, the counting rule, and the number of people in T-35. Fewer than 5 clicks means 4 at most, not 5.

values.Issue / risk: What the backup and recovery requirement covers
values.Source gap or constraint: The time zone for the daily schedule is not set; What the backup includes is not set; The kinds of failure, and what happens to a save that was in flight, are not set
values.Proposed control / decision: Approve the daily schedule, the list of stores, and the failure cases. Data that was already saved stays. A save that was in flight has an explicit outcome.

values.Issue / risk: What the privacy and encryption requirement covers
values.Source gap or constraint: The encryption standard, who holds the keys, and how long evidence is kept are not set; Who may consent, and for what, is not set; Encryption by itself does not prove FERPA compliance
values.Proposed control / decision: Approve the rules for data in transit, data at rest, and keys, and approve what students are allowed to see. The privacy owner reviews the FERPA intent separately.

values.Issue / risk: Which accessibility standard to use

values.Issue / risk: Paired courses are enforced from the catalog when the plan is saved
values.Source gap or constraint: Saving a term used to skip courses that must be taken together. Save and submit now follow the catalog corequisite text. A direction the seed adds only so the pair can be chosen together is not a requirement. PHYS 241 also requires MATH 132.
values.Proposed control / decision: Enforce each catalog direction on save and on submit. One-way pairs, including the CST labs and CHEM 110, require the lab's lecture. values.Proposed control / decision: An academic reviewer settles the policy and the text. Add tests for standing, consent, and the broken CST 300 text before calling FR-05 covered.

values.Proposed control / decision: Approve whether a planned course can count before it is taken. Enforce the grade and date rules. T-58 and T-59 cover the boundary and the fixtures.

values.Issue / risk: Idle timeout is not set
values.Source gap or constraint: lib/auth.ts has no 30-minute idle session setting; No idle listener was found in the app; See source note R-01
values.Proposed control / decision: Check the real session behavior against the 30-minute requirement. Add the handling if it is missing.

values.Source gap or constraint: Only the real academic dates in the seed can be used; While Fall 2026 is current, the next term offered is Spring 2027; There is no Fall 2027 row; See source note R-04
values.Proposed control / decision: Use the fixed test dates and the semesters that exist. Do not assume a future term, or a screen for switching programs.

values.Issue / risk: Running the seed changes shared data
values.Source gap or constraint: seed.ts deletes prerequisite groups and replaces curricula; It removes stale catalog years and may reassign student profiles; See source note R-02
values.Proposed control / decision: Run the seed only in a disposable database, after a snapshot. The count of 199 courses is for a clean database. It is not a certificate that a live database matches.

values.Source gap or constraint: The PDF coursework adds up to 117 credits; The live Information Technology total is 120, with 12 technical; The Information Technology technical pool is any CST course and can include CST 101; The generated management pool includes required MGMT 110; See source notes R-05 and R-06

values.Issue / risk: A submitted plan is not rechecked, and two saves can race
values.Source gap or constraint: Submission only checks that the plan is not empty; Approval checks the role, the status, and the PIN, not the academic rules; The write lock is checked before the transaction; See source notes R-03 and R-07
values.Proposed control / decision: Recheck the rules when the plan is submitted and when it is reviewed. Test a stale write from a second tab. Do not approve an invalid plan quietly.

values.Issue / risk: The save deadline and the failure path are untested
values.Source gap or constraint: There is no explicit 15-second timeout; Some database exceptions are passed straight through; A lecture and lab are inserted in one transaction, but the rollback and the error on the screen have not been tested; See source note R-03
values.Proposed control / decision: Run the timeout and failure tests. Confirm the pair rolls back together, and that the person sees an error and a screen that matches what was saved.

values.Issue / risk: Backups and encryption have to be proved outside the app
values.Source gap or constraint: The application source cannot prove a daily provider backup; It also cannot prove the encryption or key policy; Redis was not found in the runtime that was reviewed; See source note R-10
values.Proposed control / decision: List the stores that actually hold the data. Collect sanitized proof of backup, restore, and encryption from the provider. Do not invent a Redis or S3 setup.
